name: Albania
summary: Independent from the Ottoman Empire in 1912; under Enver Hoxha (1944–85) one of the world’s most isolated communist states; a democracy since 1991.

knownFor.label: Bunkers
knownFor.note: Over 170,000 concrete bunkers built under Hoxha.

knownFor.label: Butrint
knownFor.note: Ancient city, a World Heritage Site.

location.value: The Balkans on the Adriatic and Ionian seas.

terrain.value: Mountain ranges such as the Albanian Alps, with fertile lowland plains along the coast.

climate.value: Varied: the coast is warmest, while the northern and eastern mountains are coldest.

resources.value: Oil and gas deposits; bitumen mined at Selenicë since ancient times.

population.value: About 2.4 million (2023 census), down from 2.8 million in 2011.

urbanisation.value: Tirana is the capital and largest city, followed by Durrës, Vlorë and Shkodër; one of Europe’s fastest-urbanising countries since 1991.

disease.value: Life expectancy at birth is 77.8 years.

migration.value: Emigration since the fall of communism (1991) has helped shrink the population.

economicBase.value: Services, manufacturing and tourism (over 11 million visitors in 2024); agriculture is about 18.5% of the economy.

tradeRoutes.value: The Port of Durrës is the busiest and largest seaport.

inequality.value: Rural poverty and emigration remain issues.

governmentType.value: A parliamentary constitutional republic (since 1998), with a ceremonial president and a prime minister.

keyRulers.value: King Zog I (from 1928). Enver Hoxha (communist leader). Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Governments change through elections, held since 1991.

institutions.value: A parliament and a justice reform programme that began in 2016.

eliteConflict.value: A long rivalry between the Socialist Party and the Democratic Party.

majorWars.value: Italian invasion (1939); partisans liberated Albania from German occupation (1944).

territoryChange.value: Independence from the Ottoman Empire was declared in 1912, and the borders were set in 1913.

alliancesRivals.value: EU candidate (since 2014, negotiating since 2022); NATO member (2009).

scienceEducation.value: About half of university professors and scientists left Albania between 1991 and 2005.

openness.value: Increasingly isolationist under Hoxha, severely restricting contact with the outside world.

communicationTransport.value: A rail network run by Hekurudha Shqiptare; main seaport at Durrës.

religion.value: Secular, with no official religion; in 1976 Albania became the world’s first constitutionally atheist state.

languageWriting.value: Albanian, whose standard form merges the Gheg and Tosk dialects.

artsArchitecture.value: The historic centres of Berat and Gjirokastër are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

socialStructure.value: About 91% Albanian (2023 census), with small Greek, Roma and other minorities.

sharedIdentity.value: Skanderbeg, who resisted the Ottomans in the 1400s, is the national hero.

dailyLife.value: A strong coffee culture, with more coffee houses per person than any other country.

ideasReligions.value: Religious tolerance among Muslims, Orthodox and Catholics; the communists banned religion in 1967.

colonisation.value: Part of the Ottoman Empire for about four centuries until independence in 1912.

peakPeriod.value: Recent growth in tourism has boosted the economy.

outcome.value: Albania continues as an independent republic.
